caisi.01.quote: CAISI, which operates within NIST at the Department of Commerce
caisi.01.note: Public funding floors at 3 (F.9). Note: csa-caisi and csa-caisi-five-labs are the same URL; csa-caisi is marked unaudited while five-labs is confirmed. Both fetch fine today.

caisi.02.quote: completed more than 40 evaluations — including assessments of frontier models not yet available to the public
caisi.02.note: Government testing agreements: 3 (A.4). The CSA note does not mention TRAINS or classified work; that part of the claim is unsupported by the cited source.

caisi.03.quote: repositioned the center as CAISI, shifting emphasis toward national security and cybersecurity risk reduction

caisi.04.quote: voluntary agreements, unclassified evaluations, no mandatory disclosure of findings
caisi.04.note: Strict R.4 reading is cap 2, not 1: the public body has published per-model findings (DeepSeek V4 Pro results; ChatGPT Agent and Constitutional Classifier write-ups per the same source), so "nothing per model" (1) does not hold; most partner-lab results stay inside government, which is the anchor-2 case. Mechanism tagged statutory (R.4). Stored value 1 would move to 2.

caisi.05.bound_note: Section 9 (mis-dimensioned fact): delegating evaluations to a lab-owned contractor is not a personnel fact; none of the P anchors (board seats, equity, advisory roles, hiring) describes it. Informational on P; re-recorded on X as new signal caisi.16 (X.6).
caisi.05.quote: Scale AI SEAL : Safety, Evaluation, and Alignment Lab; first third-party evaluator authorized by US AISI
caisi.05.note: Meta's 49% stake is not in either cited source; added cnbc-scale-meta (existing confirmed record: "Meta has a 49% stake in Scale AI after investing $14.3 billion into the startup"). Rule gap: outsourcing to a lab-owned vendor has no home in P.

caisi.06.quote: The government defines the risk domains it wants evaluated
caisi.06.note: Voluntary agreements: 3 (S.4). Weak source: the span is Scale AI's proposed framework, not a description of CAISI practice; the CSA note ("jointly scoped") is the better description and is carried by caisi.13.

caisi.07.quote: CAISI published a write-up on how AI models can cheat on agentic evaluations
caisi.07.note: Methods reach the public as prose write-ups and guidelines: cap 2 (M.2). The span supports the "partly published" half; the absence of per-evaluation methods cannot be quoted.

caisi.08.quote: lead unclassified evaluations of AI capabilities that may pose risks to national security
caisi.08.note: Anchor 4 matches a NIST center. Added csa-caisi-five-labs (press, confirmed) as the non-self second source for C16. X.7's bounded "no commercial products" statement does not exist for a public body (rule gap, same as ukaisi.10). Capped at 3 anyway by new signal caisi.16 (X.6).

caisi.09.note: Leadership changed more than once in twelve months: cap 3 (G.5). The appropriation half of the claim is quoted; the resignation is carried by caisi.11.

caisi.10.quote: As of FY2026, CAISI has approximately $15 million in funding: $10 million from FY2026 appropriations
caisi.10.note: Free pre-deployment access from five labs is undisclosed in-kind on which the evaluator depends (CSA: authority "rests entirely on voluntary participation"): cap 3 (F.2, F.9). No confirmed bounded negative on lab money, so no 4 (F.12). Under the amended F.2/F.11, undisclosed in-kind sets no funding bound unless the evaluator itself states a dependency; the cap here rests on F.9 (no confirmed bounded negative; lab in-kind present), which is why the rule code is F.9.

caisi.11.quote: resigned from his role as director just three months after he was picked for the job
caisi.11.note: Third leadership change in six months: cap 3 (G.5). Quote is on the CNBC page, not the IFP page.

caisi.12.quote: provide CAISI with model access that includes versions with safety guardrails stripped back
caisi.12.note: Government testing agreements: 3 (A.4); guardrails-off access on its own is anchor 2. Mechanism lab-controlled (voluntary agreements; A.3).

caisi.13.quote: CAISI’s authority to conduct these evaluations rests entirely on voluntary participation
caisi.13.note: Voluntary memoranda: 3 (S.4). By anchor text alone "jointly scoped" reads as 2 (scope negotiated per engagement); S.4 is the tie-break for public bodies.

new_sources.title: 18 U.S. Code § 208 - Acts affecting a personal financial interest
new_sources.note: Federal criminal conflict-of-interest statute binding NIST employees: bars participation in matters in which the employee has a financial interest. Typed filing as a primary legal instrument hosted by a third party. Fetched 2026-09-15; span present.

new_sources.title: 18 U.S. Code § 207 - Restrictions on former officers, employees, and elected officials
new_sources.note: Federal post-employment statute: permanent, two-year and one-year restrictions on former executive-branch employees. Typed filing as a primary legal instrument hosted by a third party. Fetched 2026-09-15; span present.

new_signals.claim: CAISI staff are NIST federal employees bound by the criminal conflict-of-interest statute (18 U.S.C. 208) and the post-employment statute (18 U.S.C. 207), which restricts former employees for one to two years after leaving.
new_signals.quote: within 1 year after the termination of his or her service or employment as such officer or employee
new_signals.note: Statutory post-employment rules count as cooling-off (P.3); the conflict statute is a published mandatory recusal rule (P.5). Ties are disclosed on OGE forms, not publicly, so 3 not 4 (P.8). Replaces the unevidenced P value that would result from caisi.05 being informational.

new_signals.claim: CAISI is a NIST center whose staff are bound by the federal conflict-of-interest statute, 18 U.S.C. 208.
new_signals.quote: 18 U.S. Code § 208 - Acts affecting a personal financial interest
new_signals.note: Statutory civil-service conflict rules count as a conflict policy for a public body (G.2): floor 3. G.7 four needs an independent board and external review; none.

new_signals.claim: CAISI partnered with Scale AI in February 2025 to jointly develop evaluation methods for frontier models, and authorized Scale SEAL as a third-party evaluator; Meta has held 49% of Scale AI since June 2025.
new_signals.quote: Scale partnered with the U.S. Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), jointly developing new evaluation methods
new_signals.note: Co-producing evaluations with a vendor owned by a lab caps X at 3 (X.6); 49% exceeds the 20% control threshold used in F.1 and G.6. The partnership predates the Meta stake; whether it continued after June 2025 is a document request.

resolution.note: caisi.08 floors X at 4 on legal form; caisi.16 caps at 3 because CAISI co-develops evaluation methods with Scale AI, 49% owned by Meta. X.6 is the specific rule and decides: 3.

dissent.lower: Publication (R) at 2 could be 1. For the five partner labs, no per-model evaluation has been published; the public write-ups concern a foreign model tested without cooperation and two vulnerability disclosures the labs had already fixed. CSA records "no mandatory disclosure of findings". Under R.4, a public body that publishes nothing per model for the labs it has agreements with scores 1, and the DeepSeek report is the exception rather than the practice.
dissent.higher: Publication (R) at 2 could be 3. CAISI has published a full per-model evaluation (DeepSeek V4 Pro), named vulnerabilities in ChatGPT Agent and Anthropic's Constitutional Classifiers, and states that it publishes findings from its assessments. No lab-edited summary or lab redaction is documented. That is closer to anchor 3 (publishes, redaction limited to security) than to the anchor-2 picture of broad lab redaction.

resolution.note: The specific co-production rule (X.6) decides over the general legal-form floor: 3.
